title: Use the Aus Salary Calculator to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with the aus salary calculator. Compare National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax. Free tool for Australian workers.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, with super paid on top and tax deducted according to the 2026–27 resident rates.

faqs.q: How do I use the aus salary calculator to convert my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate into the timesheet on the home page. The calculator automatically multiplies by the hours you work per week (default 38) and by 52 weeks to give your annual gross pay. You can tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top of your base rate. The result shows your fortnightly pay, annual super, and estimated tax and take-home pay.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries or occupations, and they often include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. The aus salary calculator lets you enter your actual hourly rate, which may be an award rate, but it does not assume a job median. If you are using an industry or state average from reference tables, note that it is an average, not your job's median.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied in the calculator?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. In the calculator, you tick the 'casual loading' checkbox, and it adds 25% to the base rate you entered. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator adds it for you. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour, which is $26.44 plus 25%.

bodyMarkdown:
## Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with the Aus Salary Calculator

Whether you are negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, knowing your annual pay from an hourly rate is essential. The [aus salary calculator](/) on this site does the maths for you: enter your hourly rate, choose your hours per week, and instantly see your annual gross, fortnightly pay, super, and estimated tax. This article explains the formula, the assumptions, and how the National Minimum Wage compares to award rates.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard conversion is straightforward: annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. The calculator assumes a 38-hour week by default, which is the full-time ordinary hours used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours field. For a fortnightly figure, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, an hourly rate of $30.00 gives a weekly pay of $1,140.00 (30 × 38) and a fortnightly pay of $2,280.00.

This formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for estimating your annual earnings.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the minimum pay for employees not covered by a registered award or enterprise agreement. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. For casual employees, the 25% loading brings it to $33.05 per hour.

However, most Australian workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Manufacturing Award each have specific pay classifications. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site provides the current National Minimum Wage, but it is not a job median. If you are using an industry or state average from the [reference tables](/data), note that it is an average, not the median for your specific job. The aus salary calculator lets you enter your actual hourly rate, which may be an award rate, and the calculator will apply the same formula.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on your base rate. The calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading**; the calculator adds it for you. For example, if your base award rate is $28.00, tick the casual loading box, and the calculator uses $35.00 per hour.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). The calculator estimates super at 12% of your annual gross pay, but it stops applying super once your earnings exceed that cap. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

The calculator estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The result is an estimate, not a determination of your actual tax liability. For a more detailed breakdown, see the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using the Aus Salary Calculator for Your Situation

To get started, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. The calculator will show:
- Weekly pay (hourly × hours per week)
- Fortnightly pay (weekly × 2)
- Annual gross pay (weekly × 52)
- Annual super (12% of gross, capped)
- Estimated annual tax and Medicare
- Estimated annual take-home pay

You can also explore the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page for more details on the formula, or the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for information on when loading applies.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Conclusion

The aus salary calculator is a practical tool for converting your hourly rate to annual pay, whether you are comparing a salary offer or checking your own earnings. By understanding the formula and the assumptions, you can make informed decisions about your work and finances. Remember that award rates often exceed the National Minimum Wage, and casual loading adds 25% on top. Use the calculator to see how your pay stacks up.
